Note::pack¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

std::vector<std::byte> Note::pack() const

Encode The Complete Note State¶

pack() serializes a Note into an owning, versioned byte vector. It is the closed Note boundary for caches, files, messages, and other systems that carry bytes rather than C++ objects. The inverse factory is pluss::note::unpack().

The encoding preserves more than displayed values: defined state, dtype, rank, every extent, flat lane order, embedded zero bytes, and exact native numeric bits all survive a round trip. A rank-2 empty Note therefore remains rank 2, and -0.0 does not become 0.0. Text and Bytes remain different dtypes even when their lane bytes happen to match.

Version 1 begins with a 40-byte header. Its PNOT magic, version, dtype, rank, flags, element count, and three extent slots are encoded in a defined little-endian layout. Text and Bytes payloads are length-delimited; Bool uses canonical zero/one bytes; Int64 and Float64 store exact 64-bit patterns. Callers should treat this as a format contract and use unpack() rather than manually decoding or constructing envelopes.

The returned vector owns its bytes and is independent of the Note. Encoding is O(numel + payload bytes) and necessarily allocates the complete envelope. pack() performs no compression, encryption, authentication, or text normalization. Apply those concerns around the returned bytes when persistence or transport requires them.

Example 1: Inspect A Matrix Envelope And Round Trip It¶

const auto source = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::int64_t>{-1, 0, 7, 9},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto encoded = source.pack();

std::cout << "magic=";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < 4; ++i)
  std::cout << static_cast<char>(std::to_integer<unsigned char>(encoded[i]));
std::cout << " version=" << std::to_integer<unsigned>(encoded[4])
          << " rank=" << std::to_integer<unsigned>(encoded[6])
          << " bytes=" << encoded.size() << '\n';
std::cout << "restored=" << pluss::note::unpack(encoded) << '\n';

Output¶

magic=PNOT version=1 rank=2 bytes=72
restored=Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, dtype=Int64)
[
  [-1, 0], 
  [7, 9]
]

The 32-byte payload contains four exact Int64 lanes after the 40-byte header.

Example 2: Undefined Is A Serializable State¶

const auto encoded = pluss::Note::undefined().pack();
const auto restored = pluss::note::unpack(encoded);

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "undefined bytes=" << encoded.size()
          << " restored-defined=" << restored.defined() << '\n';

Output¶

undefined bytes=40 restored-defined=false

Undefined is not encoded as an empty Text Note. Its state is explicit in the header.

Example 3: Empty Geometry Keeps Its Rank¶

const auto empty = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{}, std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 0});
const auto encoded = empty.pack();
const auto restored = pluss::note::unpack(encoded);

std::cout << "empty bytes=" << encoded.size()
          << " shape=[" << restored.size(0) << ", " << restored.size(1)
          << "]\n";

Output¶

empty bytes=40 shape=[2, 0]

No payload is needed, but the header still carries Text dtype and both extents.

Example 4: Floating-Point Bits Are Not Reformatted¶

const auto source = pluss::note::make(std::vector<double>{
    -0.0, std::bit_cast<double>(UINT64_C(0x7ff8000000000000))});
const auto restored = pluss::note::unpack(source.pack());

std::cout << std::hex << std::setfill('0')
          << "float bits=0x" << std::setw(16)
          << std::bit_cast<std::uint64_t>(restored.reals()[0])
          << ",0x" << std::setw(16)
          << std::bit_cast<std::uint64_t>(restored.reals()[1]) << '\n';

Output¶

float bits=0x8000000000000000,0x7ff8000000000000

This is why pack() is suitable for exact Note round trips while printed text is not.

Failure And Trust Boundary¶

pack() validates that the in-memory Note has a supported closed dtype and geometry before writing. unpack() performs the adversarial checks: bad magic, unknown versions or dtype tags, inconsistent shapes, truncated payloads, invalid Bool lanes, overflow, and trailing bytes are rejected with pluss::Error. A successful decode owns fresh Note storage and does not borrow the encoded span.
